guide.summary: Public connection OAuth is documented for installs into other workspaces. Create a public connection with only Read content enabled, authorize one representative test user who shares one test page, then run title and markdown read tests. Installation scope is fixed at creation. The Notion-Version value and token exchange parameters are not in the supplied sources and must be confirmed before the first authorized call.
guide.recommendation: Proceed with a public connection, conditional on confirming the Notion-Version value and token exchange details from the Authorization guide. Keep Insert content and Update content disabled. Each customer must authorize individually and pick pages in the page picker. Run the two read tests after the test-user authorization succeeds.
guide.nextAction: In the Developer portal, create a public connection with only Read content enabled and choose its installation scope. Then read the Authorization guide to confirm token exchange details and the Notion-Version value before the first authorization test.

findings.title: Public connection OAuth is documented for other workspaces
findings.detail: Public connections are OAuth connections that users install into their own workspaces, and each authorizing user receives their own token.
findings.appliesWhen: Other customer organizations or workspaces connect to the app.

evidence.quote: A public connection is an OAuth connection that users install into their Notion workspaces. Unlike internal connections , which are scoped to a single workspace with a static token, public
connections follow the OAuth 2.0 protocol: each user who authorizes the connection receives their own access token, scoped to their workspace.

findings.title: Installation scope is fixed at creation
findings.detail: Any workspace allows any Notion user to install and is Marketplace-eligible. Selected workspaces only requires choosing workspaces up front and is not Marketplace-eligible. The scope cannot be changed later.

evidence.quote: Any workspace Any Notion user, in any workspace. Yes
Selected workspaces only Only the workspaces you select at creation time. No

findings.detail: Page titles and page markdown both need the Read content capability. No write capability is needed for this read-only use case.

findings.detail: Insert content would allow creating pages and Update content would allow updating pages, so both must stay off to honor the no-write rule.

findings.title: Each customer authorizes individually and picks pages
findings.detail: Each user who wants the connection must complete the authorization flow, and each person selects which pages to share through the page picker.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer user or workspace member uses the connection.

After a user authorizes a public connection, only that user can interact with the connection in their workspace. If multiple members in a workspace want to use the same public
connection, each user needs to complete the authorization flow individually.

findings.detail: Marketplace listing details are managed separately. Listing is only relevant if you choose to list on the Marketplace, which requires Any workspace scope.

steps.title: Create a public connection in the Developer portal
steps.detail: Enter the connection name, development workspace, redirect URI and installation scope. The installation scope cannot be changed later.
steps.doneWhen: The connection appears under Public connections with the redirect URI and installation scope saved.

steps.title: Set Read content only and store OAuth client credentials
steps.detail: In the Configuration tab, enable Read content and leave Insert content and Update content off. Store the client ID and secret outside source code. Capability changes make users re-authenticate.
steps.doneWhen: Capabilities show only Read content, and the client ID and secret are stored in a secrets manager.

steps.title: Authorize a representative test user and select one test page
steps.detail: As the test user, open the authorization URL from the Configuration tab, select one test page in the page picker, approve, and confirm the code exchange returns a user token. Authorization is setup, not a resource action.
steps.doneWhen: The token exchange succeeds for the test user and the token is stored for the next calls.

steps.title: Test title read on the shared test page
steps.detail: Call Retrieve a page with a title filter using the test user's token. Expect HTTP 200 with a page object whose properties include the title. Boundary check: a page the test user has not shared should return 404.
steps.doneWhen: The shared test page returns 200 with its title property, and an unshared page returns 404.

evidence.quote: ​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .
string required The ID of the page to retrieve.

string[] Property names or IDs to include in each page's properties object. Other properties are left out. Repeat the parameter to pass more than one value, for example filter_properties=title&filter_properties=Status .

steps.title: Test markdown content read on the shared test page
steps.detail: Call Retrieve page markdown with markdown_version v2 using the same test token. Expect HTTP 200 with a markdown body. Without the Read content capability, the call returns 403.
steps.doneWhen: The shared test page returns 200 with markdown content, and the read content capability is confirmed as the required permission.

evidence.quote: Set the markdown_version query parameter to v2 to get Notion-flavored Markdown instead. v2 is recommended. v1 is deprecated. It’s the default on current Notion-Versions. See Markdown versions .

blockers.title: Token exchange details are in the Authorization guide
blockers.resolution: Implement the code-to-token exchange following the Authorization guide linked from the public connections page before running the authorization test.

blockers.title: Choose installation scope before creating the connection
blockers.resolution: Choose Any workspace if customer workspaces are not known in advance. Choose Selected workspaces only if you can list them at creation. The scope cannot be changed later.

blockers.title: Confirm no write capabilities are enabled
blockers.resolution: In the Capabilities section, confirm Insert content and Update content are off and only Read content is on.
